rename.from: vagrant with ansible provisioner generates inventory file with ssh port instead winrm port for windows box
rename.to: Ansible provisioner should support WinRM settings

body:
Thanks @lenaten for filing this issue. The Ansible provisioner was created long before the support for [Windows was added to Ansible capabilities](http://www.ansible.com/blog/windows-is-coming). 

Of course your request is valid and accepted. It will be handy in the future to instruct/detect when the guest VM is a Windows box, and therefore apply ad-hoc WinRM connectivity at Ansible level. I updated the issue title in this way and assign it to myself, but, please @lenaten (or anyone interested), feel free to announce if you want to work on a PR for that change.

For now, I think that you should be able to work around this issue with some extra variables to force the [Windows connection settings](http://docs.ansible.com/intro_windows.html):

``` ruby
config.vm.provision "ansible" do |ansible|
  ansible.playbook = "provisioning/playbook.yml"
  # ...
  ansible.extra_vars = {
    ansible_ssh_user: "Administrator",
    ansible_ssh_pass: "SecretPasswordGoesHere",
    ansible_ssh_port: 5986,
    ansible_connection: "winrm"
  }
end
```

**Note:** So far, I haven't the time to verify myself, but I'll try to setup some Windows Guest VM within the next weeks and will give you some more news then. Please post us the results of your own experiments :wink:

thanks @gildegoma, in the meantime I fixed it with ugly patch.
extra_vars is not enough in my case, because I have both, windows and linux machines.  
I hope I fix it's soon with prettier code that I can share..

@lenaten good to know, that would be awesome to receive a pull request from you :heart: :heart: :heart: !

In the meantime, can you confirm that the above workaround would work for a single Windows VM? If not, could you please share some more hints?

I am also blocked by this.
Ansible extra vars do not work for some reason that I cannot tell.
Windows 7 and windows 10 guests.
Than you for looking into it!

issue.title: Support Ansible “Local Playbooks”

repository.name: vagrant
repository.description: Vagrant is a tool for building and distributing development environments.

issue.body:
At the moment, the Ansible provisioner only supports running Ansible running over SSH. IMHO, this complicates the setup and requires Ansible on the host system (unlike the Puppet provisioner, for example).

Ansible supports running playbooks on localhost: http://www.ansibleworks.com/docs/playbooks2.html#id20

issue.title: Add WinRM support to Ansible provisioner

repository.name: vagrant
repository.description: Vagrant is a tool for building and distributing development environments.

issue.body:
With this change, the Vagrant machines configured with the `:winrm` communicator will be accordingly configured in the auto-generated Ansible inventory.

Solve #5086.

Known Issues:
- when `force_remote_user = false`, the vagrant ssh username is used as default username (via the `--user` argument). This could be improved, but it sounds to me to be an an additional burden to something that can easily be fixed by setting `config.ssh.username` to the same value as `config.winrm.username`. See de96b54272f0d7eb717df0f5d7d2c065cd8b1786

@sneal @sethvargo @mitchellh review + merge please :)

body:
PR created: #6576, Feedbacks **welcome**!

So far, I ran some tests with a `Vagranfile` like this:

``` ruby
Vagrant.configure(2) do |config|

  config.winrm.transport = :ssl
  config.winrm.ssl_peer_verification = false

  config.vm.define 'trusty' do |machine|
    machine.vm.box = "ubuntu/trusty64"
  end

  config.vm.define 'win8' do |machine|
    machine.vm.box = "my_win_box"
    machine.vm.communicator = "winrm"
  end

  config.vm.provision "ansible" do |ansible|
    ansible.playbook = 'playbook-5086.yml'
    ansible.groups = { "windows" => ['win8'], "linux" => ['trusty'] }
  end

end
```

And the generated ansible inventory looks something like:

```
# Generated by Vagrant

win8 ansible_connection=winrm ansible_ssh_host=127.0.0.1 ansible_ssh_port=55986 \
ansible_ssh_user='vagrant' ansible_ssh_pass='vagrant'
trusty ansible_ssh_host=127.0.0.1 ansible_ssh_port=2222 ansible_ssh_user='vagrant' \
ansible_ssh_private_key_file='/.../.vagrant/machines/trusty/virtualbox/private_key'

[windows]
win8

[linux]
trusty
```

By forcing the `ansible_connection` mode in the inventory, there is no need to change anything in the `ansible-playbook` arguments.
If you want to use a static custom inventory, then you'll have either to set `ansible_connection=winrm` in your inventory, or as via the `raw_arguments` array.

:warning: :question: Please tell me if this is enough for your desired usages...

Notes: 

Ansible 1.9 does not seem to support WinRM in `:plaintext` mode (but it's coming in Ansible 2). For a basic/unsafe `winrm-ssl` environment, I had to monkey patch my ansible installation with a custom `callback_plugins` to skip the SSL certificate validation (see ansible/ansible#10294).

:syringe: If you have more advanced examples, please share them!

@lenaten @mihai-satmarean @nirving-versent could you please confirm if you're going to check #6576 until this Friday. I need your feedback asap, because the vagrant release is planned for next Monday.
